sub_scenario.family: communicating uncertainty and risk escalation in cross-functional decisions
sub_scenario.one_line: service design researcher: accept only with explicit uncertainty safeguards

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the research notebook and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The interview calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I facilitated a scheduled interview when the participant brief was complete.
Was the finding still tentative?
No, the session followed a prepared guide.
Someone new shadowed me in the insight studio this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the discovery sprint into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

During a vendor-complaint discovery sprint, I labeled each interview quote as observed, inferred, or open in the research notebook before proposing a follow-up owner at the insight-studio review; the program team scoped the next test instead of rewriting the script.
What did the labels accomplish?
They kept the group from treating a hunch as a settled product explanation.
I filed synthesis notes after a closed usability review last week.
Did that involve live escalation?
No, it was a standard write-up.
I archived last cycle's notes on the interview calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The proposed 15:30 office hour is on the interview calendar, and the five-minute evidence-check slot begins at 15:25.
Are those times confirmed?
Yes, they are on the sprint schedule.
A vendor call about the research notebook ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the insight studio checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the discovery sprint.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the interview calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
In an April vendor-complaint review, I committed to a product explanation before separating interview quotes from team inference, and the group built the wrong follow-up script.
What were you expected to deliver?
A definitive owner before the evidence categories were visible.
I sketched next week's plan for the discovery sprint before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the research notebook updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The research calendar leaves a 10:30 slot for next-day evidence review, and the deferral form permits moving unverified cases to that window.
Is that arrangement authorized?
Yes, both the slot and deferral field are listed.
A senior designer said saying yes immediately would show that I can handle pressure.
Did that add interview records?
No, it was about appearing responsive.
I closed the week by updating the insight studio handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How am I likely to respond to the proposed 15:30 escalation hour if it includes an evidence check and a next-morning follow-up slot?
